papers.abstract: Parallel Tempering on Boundary Conditions (PTBC) mitigates topological freezing by exchanging configurations between replicas that interpolate between periodic and open boundaries on a small defect. We generalize PTBC by replacing the instantaneous swap with a short out-of-equilibrium protocol, in which the defect couplings of two replicas are exchanged gradually while the fields around the defect are updated. We show that the swap rate depends only on the average work spent along the out-of-equilibrium trajectory by virtue of Crooks' and Jarzynski's fluctuation relations. From the theoretical derivation of the scaling of the work as a function of the number of replicas, protocol length, and defect size, we predict the swap rate and the optimal protocol length. These predictions are tested in the $2d$ $\mathrm{CP}^{N-1}$ model with $N=21$. The optimal setup agrees with the measured one, the total computational cost at fixed statistical precision decreases by $\gtrsim40\%$ with respect to standard PTBC for all explored lattice spacings, and the required number of replicas at fixed acceptance is halved.
authors: C. Bonanno, A. Bulgarelli, E. Cellini, R. Dionisio, A. Nada, D. Panfalone, D. Vadacchino, L. Verzichelli

papers.title: Robin--Hadamard states for unstable field in half-Minkowski spacetime
papers.abstract: We investigate the quantization of a real massless scalar field in four-dimensional half-Minkowski spacetime subject to an attractive Robin boundary condition. We show that the unstable modes, required for classical spectral completeness, are also essential to recover the canonical commutation relations (CCR) of the complete quantum field. By specifying the Cauchy covariances of the unstable sector, we construct a family of positive quasifree states compatible with the conservation of total energy. Within this family, positivity is incompatible with stationarity, so that the resulting states necessarily break the time-translation symmetry of the background. We also obtain a closed position-space representation of the two-point function for the chosen stable vacuum sector, including the contribution fixed by the CCR in the unstable sector. The resulting expression exhibits the direct and reflected singularities, including Robin-dependent logarithmic terms. Since the remaining unstable contribution is smooth, all states in the constructed family share the same singularity structure, consistent with the Robin--Hadamard framework.
authors: Bruno S. Felipe, Jo\~ao P. M. Pitelli, Claudio Dappiaggi

papers.title: Planckian bounds on thermalization times of strongly coupled open quantum systems
papers.abstract: We consider whether the thermalization of strongly coupled open quantum systems, whose equilibrium state is the mean-force Gibbs (MFG) state, is constrained by a fundamental Planckian time scale, $\hbar/k_B T$. By requiring that the same process thermalizes a family of nearby system Hamiltonians, we obtain a lower bound on the thermalization time, irrespective of the specific system-bath dynamics. The bound depends only on the distinguishability of the corresponding MFG states, and can therefore be computed from equilibrium properties alone. In its simplest form, it requires only a static susceptibility and an equilibrium variance of a system observable. We characterize this bound from weak to strong coupling in exactly solvable fermionic models, in the spin-boson model, and in a spin coupled to a two-dimensional Heisenberg antiferromagnet. These models show that strong coupling can lift the Planckian constraint when the MFG state retains little information about the system Hamiltonian, while preserving it when that information is carried by system observables with substantial equilibrium fluctuations at frequencies below $k_B T/\hbar$. The bound is complementary to open-system speed limits, since it constrains the acquisition of information rather than the preparation of the target, and can remain informative at strong coupling even when the latter become trivial.
authors: Jes\'us Jim\'enez-Rodr\'iguez, John Calsamiglia, Mart\'i Perarnau-Llobet

papers.title: Quark-Loop Corrections and Auxiliary Field-Strength Mixing in First-Order QCD
papers.abstract: In the first-order formulation of Yang-Mills theory the gluon field strength is an independent auxiliary field $F$, and the only gluon self-interaction is a momentum-independent cubic vertex. We determine how quarks, which couple only to the gauge field, act on this structure. Their divergences are multiples of $f(A)\cdot f(A)$, a term absent from the first-order Lagrangian that no rescaling can produce. Working with the background-field method in a general covariant gauge, we find that the quark sector is renormalized entirely by the mixing of the auxiliary field with the field strength known from pure Yang-Mills theory, $F_0=F+z\,f(A)$, with quark coefficient $z=-\alpha_sT_FN_f/(6\pi\bar\epsilon)$, together with a rescaling of the gluon field and no rescaling of $F$, so that the renormalized auxiliary field runs into the gluon field strength. When a heavy quark of mass $M$ is integrated out, the same mixing survives as a finite threshold coefficient $c=(\alpha_sT_F/6\pi)\ln(M^2/\mu^2)$, whose scale dependence is exactly the heavy-quark share of the running, and the invariant combination of the couplings reproduces the decoupling of $\alpha_s$. Below the threshold, when the leading power correction is kept as a gauge-sector operator, the auxiliary field is no longer the field strength: $F=f(A)+(g\alpha_sT_F/15\pi M^2)(D_\alpha J_\beta-D_\beta J_\alpha)$, with $J$ the light-quark colour current. We verify this identity against the full theory and show that it separates the long-distance gluon exchange, carried by $F$, from the short-distance heavy-quark effect, carried by a four-quark contact term.

papers.title: Native higher-order optimization with entropy quantum computing
papers.abstract: Higher-order interactions are common in applied optimization: parity checks, radar-code sidelobes, portfolio skewness and kurtosis, and marketing-channel synergies all yield cubic or quartic objectives. Quantum annealers and most Ising machines accept only quadratic objectives, and gate-based quantum processors build every higher-order term from two-qubit gates. Entropy quantum computing, realized in the hybrid photonic-electronic Dirac-3S system, accepts polynomials of degree up to five with all-to-all coupling over binary, integer or simplex-constrained continuous variables. No user-supplied quadratization or circuit compilation is needed. We formulate four industrial use cases as six cubic and quartic instances, run them on Dirac-3S with 30 samples each, and score every sample against a certified optimum or a classical best-known value. We also estimate their cost on quantum annealers, superconducting grids and trapped-ion registers under standard mappings. For the two densest instances, a portfolio with about 80,000 terms and a budget allocation with 360,000 terms, the quadratized problems need embeddings far beyond current annealers, over $10^5$ physical qubits for the portfolio alone, and one phase-separation layer costs over $10^6$ two-qubit gates before optimization. Dirac-3S ran all six natively and returned feasible, distinct solutions. All samples of the binary instances are single-flip local minima. The best portfolio sample lies within 0.32% of the best-known value and the best budget sample 15% above it, but no sample reached its reference. Classical solvers reach the references within minutes at these sizes, and random starts followed by a local polish reach comparable or better values, so the advantage established here is one of expressibility and mapping cost, not of solution quality. Whether it extends to time to solution at larger sizes remains open.
authors: Narendra N. Hegade, Pranav Chandarana, Sebastian Wagner, Bahman Qawami, Wesley Dyk

papers.title: Experimental characterisation of compilation-dependent Grover--Rudolph probability distribution loading on a three-qubit NMR processor
papers.abstract: Exact state-preparation circuits are normally judged by how closely the measured output distribution reproduces the target. Using the ancilla-free Grover-Rudolph construction compiled into {Ry, X, CNOT}, we ask instead how much the accuracy of a probability-distribution loading depends on which of several logically equivalent compilations is executed. Two Gray-code realisations of the level-2 uniformly controlled rotation, A and B, differ only in the order of their CNOT controls: same unitary, same angles. On a three-qubit liquid-state NMR processor they do not perform identically. Across 700 runs over seven targets the A/B contrast is significant for 3 of them under Holm, with no fixed sign. Two further campaigns isolate the effect within one unit. Removing the circuit's identity-equivalent gates, which changes the executed schedule but not the unitary, affects the two realisations differently: a ladder x intervention interaction of +0.0625 (95% CI [+0.0306, +0.0944], paired p = 4.8e-4), reversing the sign of the A/B advantage. Across five acquisitions of this one logical circuit the contrast runs from +0.0395 to -0.0229. Not every compilation choice matters: commanding the two level-1 inverse rotations as 720 deg - theta rather than -theta, with the gate list unchanged, moves the mean fidelity by -0.0006 ([-0.0157, +0.0146]) on one target in one session. We offer the order and timing of the executed pulses as the hypothesis these observations favour, without identifying a mechanism. The metric does not certify coherences, and the measured correlators are inconsistent with any global depolarising description: on the uniform target, at a classical fidelity of 0.962, a two-body correlation of +0.217 appears where the target has none. Run-level data and code are deposited for every campaign run on our own unit; the pulse-level campaign is reported from summary tables.
authors: Antonio Falc\'o, Daniela Falc\'o-Pomares, Juan-Carlos Latorre, Yuefeng Lin

papers.title: Graph Parameterization for Invariant Manifolds Attached to Quasi-Periodic Tori
papers.abstract: We develop a high-order Fourier-Taylor graph-parameterization method for computing local invariant manifolds attached to reducible quasi-periodic invariant tori of discrete dynamical systems, with particular emphasis on Poincar\'e maps. Assuming that the invariant torus and its Floquet reduction are known, we represent the manifold as a graph over a selected spectral subspace and compute its coefficients recursively through jet transport and cohomological equations on the torus. The formulation accommodates stable, unstable, and center spectral selections. For center manifolds, it simultaneously determines the nonlinear reduced dynamics, providing a low-dimensional representation from which nearby invariant objects can be lifted to the original phase space. For real systems with complex-conjugate Floquet multipliers, we derive an equivalent real formulation based on Hermitian symmetry and Krawtchouk transformations. This allows real-valued jet transport while retaining the advantages of complex spectral coordinates in the cohomological solver. The implementation also incorporates inverse dynamics for stable directions, multiple shooting, coordinate scaling, and a posteriori validation tests. Numerical experiments with a quasi-periodically forced pendulum, an oscillating solar sail in the Earth-Moon system, and a simplified solar system model illustrate the construction and its computational properties. In the solar-sail benchmark, the real formulation reduces computation time by approximately a factor of 2.2 compared with the complex implementation.
authors: Miquel Barcelona, Joan Gimeno, Marc Jorba-Cusc\'o

papers.title: Inverted Pendulum in the Sky: Floquet Stabilization of Cosmological Axions
papers.abstract: Many cosmological scenarios require a scalar field to sit near the top of its potential, which usually requires a fine-tuned initial condition. We ask whether the hilltop of an axion potential can be dynamically stabilized by a rapidly oscillating coupling, as for the inverted pendulum of Kapitza, and to what extent this can reduce the fine-tuning. Using Floquet theory, we determine the stability window of the hilltop and analyze several realizations: an oscillating coupling, a spinning or oscillating second field, and a gyroscopic analogue, an inverted spinning top realized by a sigma model on a squashed three-sphere. In an expanding Universe the stabilized phase lasts for a number of $e$-folds logarithmic in the hierarchy of scales, independently of the cosmological background. Classifying the stabilizers by how their effective frequency redshifts, we show that in these realizations the hilltop cannot both attract the field and leave it frozen by the Hubble friction during radiation or matter domination, and that during inflation the attraction is limited by the Hubble friction and the energy budget. Thus the simple realizations studied here do not generically remove the hilltop fine-tuning. They can instead delay the onset of the oscillation and enhance the relic abundance as $n_\phi/n_{\phi,{\rm std}}\propto(\tilde m/H_c)^{3/2}$ in radiation domination. We discuss the implications for axion dark matter, inflation, quintessence and curvatons.

papers.title: Black hole entropy from angular holonomies of Sine-Gordon soliton lattices in AdS$_3$
papers.abstract: We construct boundary conditions for AdS$_3$ gravity that realize Sine-Gordon dynamics. For a periodic soliton lattice at fixed winding, we relate the angular holonomy to the exact acoustic dispersion by continuing the Bloch momentum through the zero-frequency band edge associated with rigid translation of the lattice. For suitable embedding angles, the stable vacuum has a regular BTZ geometry. When only one chiral sector carries winding, we construct a family whose asymptotic region extends to a BTZ black hole. As the spectral parameter of the winding sector tends to the corresponding band edge, the black hole approaches extremality. The leading correction to the extremal entropy is linear in the Hawking temperature defined with respect to laboratory time, with a coefficient inversely proportional to the sound velocity of the lattice. The same inverse-velocity dependence appears in the low-temperature entropy of one-dimensional quantum fluids.
authors: Marcela C\'ardenas, Francisco Correa, Nicol\'as Salazar

papers.title: Quantum dynamics of a charged particle on rotating curved surfaces and space curves in electromagnetic fields
papers.abstract: We develop a gauge-consistent framework for a charged particle confined to a rotating curved manifold in an electromagnetic field, starting from the covariant Klein--Gordon equation. The non-relativistic reduction casts the rotational effects as effective gauge potentials while preserving the $U(1)$ symmetry, so that rotation and the external field enter alike, the geometry entering separately as the da Costa potential. The obstruction to dimensional reduction is gauge--geometry entanglement: transverse magnetic fields on a two-dimensional (2D) surface and structural torsion on a one-dimensional (1D) curve couple the tangential dynamics to the transverse degrees of freedom. We remove this entanglement by three mechanisms---a generalized transverse Poincar\'{e} gauge, the rotation-minimizing Bishop frame, and the parity of the transverse ground state, the last of which annihilates the residual first-order magnetic coupling for a single inversion-symmetric well. On a torus, an axial field generates a joint Sagnac--Aharonov--Bohm residual of tunable sign without spoiling the poloidal--azimuthal separability, whereas an in-plane field couples only through the out-of-plane extent of the structure: it breaks the axial symmetry there but leaves a planar curve unaffected to first order. The same torus shows the axial field tuning the curvature-induced localization, and a corrugated quantum ring converts periodic geometric and flux modulations into an artificial superlattice whose in-plane-field immunity follows from planarity and parity, not from the smallness of the field. Non-inertial quantum dynamics on surfaces and curves of arbitrary shape is thus reduced, within the thin-layer regime, to two ingredients: an effective gauge potential and a geometric potential.

papers.title: Exact Lyapunov spectrum and localization length of the multichannel disordered Schr\"odinger equation
papers.abstract: We consider the multichannel Schr\"odinger equation, describing the evolution of $N$ transverse modes in a finite width wire, in the presence of a Gaussian white noise potential in the unitary symmetry class. For arbitrary energy $E$ and disorder strength $T$, we compute exactly the set of Lyapunov exponents $\{ \gamma_n(E,T) \}_{1 \leq n \leq N}$ which define the decay rates of the wave functions. In the large energy regime, we recover that the Lyapunov exponents are equally spaced, as predicted by the so-called DMPK approach. However we show that this property breaks down at arbitrary energy, giving rise to a richer Lyapunov spectrum. We also uncover a direct relation between the localization length, given by the inverse of the smallest Lyapunov exponent, and the density of states. Our derivation relies on the analysis of matrix stochastic differential equation for a modified Riccati matrix.

papers.title: Uphill Diffusion in Yukawa Plasmas
papers.abstract: In a fluid mixture of many species an individual species can diffuse toward higher concentration without any external driving force because its flux is coupled to the gradients of other components. Such `uphill diffusion' is well known in the chemical and metallurgy literature but to our knowledge has not been studied for strongly coupled plasmas in neutron star and white dwarf interiors. We have previously developed a semi-analytic diffusion model that accurately predicts diffusion coefficients of individual species in a mixture in equilibrium. Uphill diffusion allows us to test this model out of equilibrium, and also test a generalized Darken relation for predicting diffusivities. We derive an analytic theory and compare to three-component molecular dynamics simulations and find very good agreement. This provides a novel out-of-equilibrium test of the generalization of our diffusion model to arbitrary multi-component mixtures.
authors: Matt E. Caplan, Evan B. Bauer, Mohammed Bettioua

papers.title: Exponential Analysis for Trace-Distance Errors in Quantum Information Theory
papers.abstract: We study the trace-distance error in classical-quantum soft covering, privacy amplification against quantum side information, convex splitting, and decoupling by a Haar-random unitary followed by partial trace. In the independent and identically distributed setting, we determine exact reliability functions and strong converse exponents for soft covering with independent codewords, uniform convex splitting, and Haar partial-trace decoupling. For privacy amplification, we determine the exact reliability function for independent random binning and the exact strong converse exponent for every two-universal hash ensemble. The reliability and strong converse formulas involve sandwiched and Petz-R\'enyi information, respectively. The proofs connect trace-distance errors to quantum hypothesis testing, using Rosenthal inequalities for sums of random matrices in the reliability analysis and conditional second-moment bounds for the strong converses.
authors: Hao-Chung Cheng, Li Gao, Shi-Bing Li, Hongsen Qiu

papers.title: Noise threshold for learning with quantum memory
papers.abstract: A quantum memory can reduce exponentially the number of experiments needed to learn a physical process, but real memories are noisy. Here we show that, for Pauli memory noise with eigenvalues $\lambda_X,\lambda_Y,\lambda_Z$, the advantage is governed by $\lambda_X^2+\lambda_Y^2+\lambda_Z^2$. We prove that no protocol with an entangled probe gains an exponential advantage when this sum is at most one, reduce the general case to the additivity of a R\'enyi-2 coherent information, and find coded memories that retain a growing advantage within 1% of this threshold. On a superconducting processor, nine simultaneously operated Bell pairs show an advantage that grows or shrinks exponentially with system size, reversing where a parameter-free model predicts. A three-qubit repetition code turns a shrinking advantage into a growing one with all processor and readout errors included, and under dephasing its memory performs better than Bell sampling in any memory frame on a perfect processor.
authors: Miaojiang Chen, Wenjing Xiao, Haiqiang Chen, Jiarong Liang, Anfeng Liu, Zhenrong Zhang, Athanasios V. Vasilakos, Saif Al-Kuwari, Ahmed Farouk, H. Herbert Song

papers.title: Conditional multiparameter thermometry with neutrino oscillations: MSW energy diversity and a plasma-noise benchmark
papers.abstract: We address temperature-parameter inference in a restricted two-flavor neutrino dephasing model with fixed mean electron densities. When two zone temperatures enter the propagated state via a single accumulated dephasing exponent, the single-energy quantum Fisher information matrix has rank at most 1. Independent, energy-resolved samples restore regular local identifiability when their thermal-sensitivity vectors are noncollinear. Matter-dependent mixing provides distinct weights in an illustrative two-zone model. A separate two-probe benchmark shows how complementary Bell sectors can distinguish temperature from spatial noise correlations. An electron-only Debye-cell estimate gives a conditional longitudinal quantum signal-to-noise ratio of approximately $3.1\times10^{-13}$ at 10 MeV for a uniform central-density medium over one solar radius. This estimate is not a microscopic upper bound or a detector sensitivity forecast. Complete phase averaging removes temperature information carried solely by longitudinal coherence damping; to retain solar sensitivity, a separate calculation of population, refractive, or production effects is required. The results distinguish conditional state identifiability from operational temperature inference.
authors: Jilali Loulijat, Abdallah Slaoui, El Hassan Saidi, Mohamed Gouighri, Berihu Teklu

papers.title: Backpropagation as Dirac-bracket dynamics of dissipative training
papers.abstract: Gradient-based training of a parametric model is the motion of a damped particle in the potential set by the loss. Using the Bateman-Galley doubling of the degrees of freedom, which gives dissipative systems an action principle, we write gradient flow, the heavy-ball method and Nesterov's accelerated gradient method as Hamiltonian systems. We show that, within this Hamiltonian description, backpropagation is Dirac evolution. The activations of a feed-forward network are treated as coordinates of phase space, and the layer equations as constraints. These constraints are second class for every architecture, and Hamilton's equations with the resulting Dirac bracket reproduce training with the exact gradient of the loss, although the Hamiltonian contains only the cost of the network output. The Dirac bracket of an activation with the momenta of the parameters is its Jacobian, the inverse of the constraint matrix contains both the forward and the reverse modes of automatic differentiation, and the errors propagated by backpropagation are the Lagrange multipliers of the layer constraints: the constraint forces of a kinematic chain under the load of the cost. These results hold in the full doubled phase space, not only in the physical limit. The network's part of the constraint algebra is the same for every optimizer, Nesterov's look-ahead adds one layer of momentum-dependent constraints that couple the two copies of the doubled system, and gradient flow is obtained by constructing the Dirac bracket in stages. We confirm these statements numerically to machine precision and train a network by integrating the Dirac flow of its constraints, with no backward pass in the computation.
authors: Nicolaus Linneu Holanda, Ivan Eugenio Cunha

papers.title: High-Throughput GPU Decoding of Quantum Bivariate Bicycle Codes under Circuit-Level Noise
papers.abstract: Bivariate bicycle (BB) codes reduce the physical-qubit overhead of quantum error correction compared to other codes such as Surface codes, but circuit-level faults create dependencies across measurement rounds that limit decoding throughput. We present a parallel-window GPU decoder that combines reusable fault patterns, compact shared-memory state, and persistent GPU workers using min-sum with Relay-BP recovery. On an RTX 5090, the proposed decoder keeps pace with one syndrome round every 1 $\mu$s across all four evaluated codes, up to [[144,12,12]] with 63-144 $\mu$s median commit delays. This rate has not been demonstrated in prior circuit-level GPU decoding studies and it provides $120\times$ higher decoding throughput than sequential sliding-window decoding. Checking neighboring detector rounds before accepting a decoding result reduces failure rates by up to 65%. For [[144,12,12]] at $p=0.002$, our proposed decoder achieves $7.58\times 10^{-6}$ failures per round, 36% lower than the published belief propagation (BP) with syndrome flipping (BP-SF) result.

papers.title: Resource theory of pi-ordered imaginarity and its resource quantifiers
papers.abstract: Conventional resource theory of quantum imaginarity takes real density matrices as free states without ordering constraints on their diagonal populations. Motivated by the role of population ordering in the incoherent ergotropy of quantum batteries and the recently proposed framework of $\pi$-ordered coherence, we develop the resource theory of $\pi$-ordered imaginarity. In this refined framework, free states are required to be real in the reference basis and to obey a prescribed permutation order $\pi$ for their diagonal populations. This theory thereby identifies two independent quantum resources: complex phases and population misordering, where the latter is inaccessible within the standard imaginarity resource theory. We characterize the structure of free states using majorization and the Schur-Horn theorem, define admissible $\pi$-ordered real operations, and examine their intersection with $\pi$-ordered incoherent operations. We further construct resource quantifiers for the $\pi$-ordered imaginarity based on relative entropy, fidelity and robustness, and derive inequalities relating the robustness of $\pi$-ordered imaginarity and that of $\pi$-ordered coherence. The present framework generalizes the standard resource theory of imaginarity to incorporate population ordering and is naturally suited for thermodynamic settings such as quantum batteries.
authors: Yanjun Chu, Yushan Ding, Yuhang Xie, Chenyang Cui, Shao-Ming Fei

papers.title: Superconformal Index Identities for Dual Gauge Theories
papers.abstract: We study superconformal index identities for three classes of dual four-dimensional gauge theories. For $\mathcal N=4$ super-Yang--Mills theory with gauge groups $SO(2n+1)$ and $USp(2n)$, we prove at every rank the equality of flavored Schur indices predicted by $S$-duality, using Rains's diagonal trace transformation. For Kutasov--Schwimmer duality with adjoint superpotential $\textrm{Tr} X^{k+1}$, we prove the index identity between $SU(k+1)$ and $SU(k-1)$ with two flavors at independent elliptic nomes $p,q$, in the ultraviolet assignment $R(Q)=0$. On the locus $p=q^k$, we reduce the identity to that of ordinary supersymmetric QCD whenever the specialized expressions are generically regular. Finally, we test the dualities conjectured by Cho and Song between quiver and single-group descriptions of four families of Argyres--Douglas theories. For the rank-one $H_1$ theory we prove equality of the two full flavored indices, and for each family at arbitrary rank we evaluate the generalized Coulomb index in both descriptions, obtaining the product formula conjectured by Buican and Jiang.
authors: Min-xin Huang, Gao-fu Ren, Xin Wang

papers.title: Dynamics of a Charged Particle on a Conformal Helicoidal Surface
papers.abstract: We study the classical and quantum motion of a charged particle on a conformal helicoidal surface embedded in four-dimensional Euclidean space. A uniform ambient magnetic field pulls back to a nonuniform surface field. The cyclic longitudinal coordinate permits an exact transverse reduction. The ordinary helicoid in the same axial field shares the effective potential and the turning points, while the conformal metric increases the physical period at matched energy and longitudinal momentum. We classify the single- and double-well regimes and obtain the exact transverse periods in the two double-well sectors. The periods diverge logarithmically at the separatrix, with twice the leading coefficient above the barrier as below it. The zero-field limit allows transverse escape, and the weak-twist limit is locally free but nonuniform across the surface. Intrinsic quantization gives an exact weighted transverse eigenvalue problem. Fixed-momentum eigenvalues test the harmonic approximation in a central well and resolve the tunneling splittings in a double well.
authors: Hassan Hassanabadi, Abdullah Guvendi, Georg Junker

papers.title: Diffusion Effects on a Stochastic Amplifier Driven by the Square of a Gaussian Field: Discontinuous Transition to Intermittency
papers.abstract: We study the effects of diffusion on the transition to intermittency in stochastic amplification driven by the square of a Gaussian field. The transition is characterized by an order parameter quantifying the spatial uniformity of the amplification. We consider a model in which the diffusion-amplification process is embedded in a random lattice of point absorbers in such a way that the Feynman-Kac formula is restricted to Brownian paths with a range not exceeding a finite cut-off. In this setting, with the Gaussian driving field in a wide class of physical interest, we show that diffusion-induced damping of the amplification is sufficiently strong to change the nature of the transition: from continuous in the absence of diffusion, to discontinuous in the presence of diffusion.

papers.title: Gravitational collapse to extremal black holes with $\Lambda>0$: counterexamples to the third law without charge
papers.abstract: We study the dynamical formation of the extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution, in both its time orientations, and the related Nariai solution. We prove that there exist spherically symmetric, regular Cauchy data for the Einstein-scalar field system with $\mathbb S^3$ topology, for any scalar field mass $\mathfrak{m}\geq 0$, that lead to the formation of an exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole in finite time, and that moreover the apparent horizon of the solution is exactly isometric to that of the subextremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution at earlier times. We also show that if the scalar field mass satisfies $\mathfrak{m}>\sqrt{\Lambda}/2$, an analogous result holds having the extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter white hole or the Nariai solution in place of the black hole. In the black hole case, the exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region is bounded to the future by two event horizons and can be seen as the analogue of the exterior region in the asymptotically flat case. We moreover establish that these two black hole horizons that bound the exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region are the only event horizons present in the spacetime, something non-trivial given the existence of multi-black hole configurations when $\Lambda > 0$. Consequently, the solutions arising from these data can be thought to constitute, in particular, regular counterexamples to the third law of black hole thermodynamics with $\Lambda>0$ arising from the collapse of physically plausible matter which is moreover uncharged. Our approach to construct the Cauchy data relies on $C^k$ characteristic gluing results for the Einstein-scalar field system in spherical symmetry, in the spirit of [KU25].

papers.title: Distribution of the ratio of the two smallest eigenphases of the Jacobi unitary ensemble
papers.abstract: We compute the joint distribution of the two smallest eigenvalues of the Jacobi unitary ensemble and the distribution of their ratio. We use a framework for calculating Janossy densities based on the Tracy-Widom system of ordinary differential equations. For the cases studied here, the leading finite-N correction to the ratio distribution, relative to its universal Bessel-kernel limit, is O(N^{-4}). This behaviour reflects a nontrivial cancellation of lower-order corrections present in the Jacobi kernel. Eigenphase ratios may thus reveal subtle finite-size effects in quantum-chaotic systems with particle-hole or chiral symmetry. As an exploratory arithmetic application, we compare the ratio distribution for the two lowest zeros of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions with the hard-edge limit for Sp(N). The data indicate that the N_{eff}^{-1} term vanishes, leaving an O(N_{eff}^{-2}) correction.

papers.title: Why do single photons produce interference fringes? The phase of a mode and the phase of a state
papers.abstract: If the phase of a photon-number state is completely undetermined, how can single photons, sent one at a time through a two-slit apparatus, build up interference fringes? These lecture notes answer this question from first principles. Starting from Maxwell's equations, we expand the field in vector modes, quantize it, and introduce the quantity measured by a photodetector. We then show that the word ``phase'' refers to two different things: the phase of a mode, fixed by the optical setup, and the phase of the quantum state that excites the mode. Only the first determines the fringes. All calculations are given in full, and problems with solutions are included.

papers.title: Measuring the Roughness of Quasi-Circular Interfaces at Finite Resolution
papers.abstract: Interface roughness characterizes the boundary fluctuations across different length scales, which can reveal information about a material''s pinning landscape and collective interfacial behaviour. Finite sampling and image resolution can bias the measured scaling properties, however. These effects can particularly complicate comparisons between circular domains of different sizes, where the number of resolved boundary points, and the relationship between angular and physical separations vary with the interface radius. Here, we benchmark the recovery of the roughness exponent and amplitude using synthetic self-affine interfaces generated by Fourier synthesis, mapped onto circular contours, and rasterized onto a pixel grid. We first compare displacement-correlation (B(r)) and structure-factor (S(q)) estimates for different interface lengths. To address non-uniform angular and radial spacing in a circular interface, we assess a reconstruction procedure that weights slope minimization against medial interface position. We find that while spectral estimates were most effective in the original interfaces, this advantage did not persist after circular mapping. Moderate smoothing was found to improve parameter recovery, but stronger smoothing can bias both the scaling exponent and roughness amplitude. These results, verified on both synthetic datasets, and an experimental ferroelectric system, identify limitations of circular-interface roughness measurements and provide a basis for further investigations into the evolution of circular domains under finite resolution experiments.
authors: Ralph Bulanadi, Asraful Haque, Sumner B. Harris, Rama Vasudevan, Yongtao Liu

papers.title: Bolognesi's Conjecture for Nonnegative-Charge Iterated Magnetic Bags
papers.abstract: We establish a magnetic-bag limit for smooth $SU(2)$ Bogomolny monopoles associated with finitely many nested smooth surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^3$. This proves Bolognesi's magnetic-bag conjecture for iterated magnetic bags with nonnegative charge density on each surface.

papers.title: Power-law tunneling in the Razavy hyperbolic double well: Heun connection formulas and their resonances
papers.abstract: We study nonperturbative level splitting in the symmetric Razavy hyperbolic double well, relating its double-confluent Heun connection problem to exact WKB and quasi-exact solvability. In the weak-coupling limit the wells separate logarithmically and approach two Morse systems. Reflection factorizes the two-ended spectral condition into separate even and odd quantization conditions. For each normalizable Morse level with noninteger decay exponent, the irregular-block connection formula yields the leading splitting with its full gamma-function coefficient, two analytic fluctuation corrections, and the leading logarithmic three-traversal contribution. The noninteger power of the coupling follows from the logarithmic growth of the barrier action. We express the classical periods in terms of complete elliptic integrals and derive the first quantum-period correction. At integer exponent, a convergent reduction onto the two resonant Floquet modes resolves the singular fixed-order expansion into two local spectral branches and reproduces the known finite-spin tunneling gap.

papers.title: Genus one mirror symmetry and surfaces with trivial first Chern class
papers.abstract: The main goal of this paper is to study the extension of genus-one BCOV type mirror symmetry for smooth projective varieties with vanishing $c_1(X)$. We show that the naive generalization of the expectation that one can encode genus one Gromov-Witten invariants in the BCOV invariant of the mirror family cannot hold in this setup. We show this by completing the study of these invariants for surfaces. Progress had been made recently by Oberdieck's proof of the Klemm-Mari\~no conjecture for Enriques surfaces, which can be combined with computations of equivariant analytic torsion by Yoshikawa. We also perform the analogous study for bielliptic surfaces. Both of these cases present a sign issue not present in the known trivial canonical bundle cases, which we show implies that the mirror symmetry predictions cannot hold for varieties with torsion canonical bundle, even up to sign.

papers.title: Stochastic Failure Dynamics in a Model Peptidoglycan Mesh under Hydrolysis and Mechanical Loading
papers.abstract: We develop a minimal stochastic-mechanical model for failure dynamics of the Gram-negative peptidoglycan (PG) cell wall under blocked growth and continued hydrolysis. The cell wall is modelled as a collection of load-bearing cross-sections, with random number of cross-links in each such cross-section, around a fixed degree of cross-linking. To understand failure dynamics of the cell wall under antibacterial agents which prevent insertion of fresh PG material, peptide bonds are progressively excised by hydrolases, while insertion/formation of new bonds is blocked. We compare and contrast rupture dynamics in no-load and load-activated regimes, using extreme value theory and stochastic simulations, deriving limiting laws for system failure in both the long-cell and large crosslinking limits. For a cross-section with many bonds, the mean failure time grows only log- arithmically with bond number, giving diminishing returns from additional cross-linking. In the no-load case, the centered failure time converges to a Gumbel law, though crucially, load changes the centered distribution and accelerates the final stages of collapse. In long cells, failure follows a weakest-link Weibull-type scaling controlled by the least cross-linked regions, with mechanical load reducing the failure-time scale without changing the weakest-link exponent. The fraction of bonds removed before failure tends to zero, showing that collapse can remain highly localized even while the global cross-linking degree stays high. Slowing down growth and other cellular functions is a typical antibiotic escape mechanism for bacteria and in this context, we show that, hydrolase down-regulation uniformly rescales the failure-time distribution and delays collapse, but does not remove the load-induced preference for rupture in weakened regions.

papers.title: The all-loop spectrum of GGK strings
papers.abstract: We study the non-perturbative spectrum of the non-relativistic limit of string theory in AdS$_5\times$S$^5$, also known as GGK theory. In light-cone gauge, we show that the bosonic spectrum on a number of vacua is described at all-loops by free massive and massless scalar fields in AdS$_2$, confirming a conjecture by de Leeuw, Fontanella and Nieto-Garc\'ia, arXiv:2403.09563. In static gauge, we obtain the same result for any classical string vacuum, and including fermions. We compute the quantum correction to the classical energy, and show that it vanishes once we adopt the regularised Hurwitz series. We conclude that the quantum energy spectrum built upon any GGK string consists solely of its classical vacuum energy.
authors: Marius de Leeuw, Andrea Fontanella, Cameron Gibson, Juan Miguel Nieto Garc\'ia

papers.title: The Zero Mode Constraint in the Dirac-Bergmann Analysis of Kadomtsev-Petviashvili Type Equations
papers.abstract: We derive the Hamiltonian formulation of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili (KP) equation from a singular Lagrangian by means of the Dirac-Bergmann algorithm. The Lagrangian contains an auxiliary field, which leads to an irregular secondary constraint. On the branch that reproduces the KP equation, all constraints are second class, and the Dirac brackets give the known Hamiltonian and Poisson operator. We confirm these results by the Faddeev-Jackiw method. Then, we consider fields periodic in the first spatial coordinate. In this case, the zero modes of the derivative operator lead to an additional secondary constraint on the mean of the potential. This constraint replaces the inverse derivative by its zero mean counterpart, and the resulting Hamiltonian is in accordance with the one of Reiman and Semenov-Tyan-Shanskii, up to normalization conventions. For decaying fields, the same condition is necessary for rapidly decreasing potentials to remain rapidly decreasing. We show that this constraint appears for a general class of KP-type equations. In addition, we classify the smooth solutions of the auxiliary-field action. We also relate our results to an existing quantization of the KP equation, for which the potential Lagrangian provides an action.

papers.title: Spectral reciprocity for reductive groups
papers.abstract: For every finite subgroup $\Gamma\subset\operatorname{SU}(2)$, every connected compact or connected complex reductive group $G$, and every finite central subgroup $B\subset Z(G)$, we construct a degree-preserving linear Fourier isomorphism between the polynomial class modules of $(G,B)$ and $((G/B)^\vee,\widehat B)$. The transform exchanges central twists with characters of the actual grades and preserves the invariant polynomial contributions of the full centralizers. In degree zero it yields central-coefficient reciprocity under the Poincar\'e pairing on $S^3/\Gamma$. In particular, $\Gamma$ admits equally many conjugacy classes of homomorphisms into $G$ and its Langlands dual, which verifies a conjecture of Kojima and Tachikawa.

papers.title: LatentRL-QAS: Transfer via Latent Reinforcement Learning for Quantum Architecture Search
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) emerges as a prominent approach to quantum architecture search (QAS), the automated design of quantum circuits. However, transferring what an agent has learned from one number of qubits to another is still weakly explored: the state, the action space and the neural network of a state-of-the-art RL-QAS agent all grow with the number of qubits, which makes transfer learning across qubit counts prohibitive. We make this transfer possible by introducing LatentRL-QAS, a latent space transfer and refresh framework for RL-based QAS. At its core, a circuit variational autoencoder encodes a circuit as one token per gate and maps circuits on any number of qubits into the same latent space. An RL agent navigates this space instead of adding gates, so its state, actions and network have the same size at every qubit count. The latent space is periodically refreshed with the agent's new discoveries and, for a larger system, grown from the solutions of the smaller one, so what is transferred is the representation of circuits, not network weights or past experience. To show transfer, we consider absolutely maximally entangled (AME) states, a resource for quantum error correction. LatentRL-QAS discovers the five- and six-qubit AME states without being shown them and prepares them in 89-99% of evaluation episodes, whereas the baseline RL-QAS fails to find them with the same budget, even with a network 10 to 17 times larger. LatentRL-QAS remains robust under depolarizing noise with single-qubit gate errors amplified 10x and two-qubit gate errors 5x compared with IBM quantum hardware. By decoupling the RL agent from the number of qubits, LatentRL-QAS lets quantum architecture search reuse circuit representations learned on smaller problems, providing a foundation for the transferable design of circuits across quantum optimization problems.
authors: Maria Ilektra Plakitsi, Sebastian Feld, Akash Kundu

papers.title: Data-enhanced self-learning projective quantum Monte Carlo with Rydberg-atom measurements
papers.abstract: We introduce a data-enhanced self-learning projective quantum Monte Carlo (PQMC) method that incorporates projective measurements from programmable quantum simulators into the guiding wavefunction of a ground-state projection. We demonstrate the approach for a two-dimensional Rydberg-atom array using restricted Boltzmann machine (RBM) and recurrent neural network (RNN) guiding wavefunctions. Experimental pretraining reduces finite-population effects and accelerates self-learning convergence, allowing unbiased estimation of ground-state properties to be obtained with fewer walkers and fewer self-learning iterations. The improvement is particularly pronounced for the RBM, while the more accurate RNN guiding wavefunction exhibits a smaller, though still observable, benefit from pretraining. Simulations across different system sizes suggest that the relative advantage of experimental pretraining may increase with system size. Improvements are also observed for the checkerboard order parameter, despite deviations of the experimental measurements from the equilibrium numerical results. Finally, finite-size scaling with self-learning PQMC without experimental pretraining yields the critical point and critical exponents of the disordered-to-checkerboard transition in agreement with previous numerical studies. Our results show that limited and imperfect experimental measurements can provide an effective initialization for self-learning PQMC, while imaginary-time projection combined with subsequent unsupervised learning progressively refines the guiding wavefunction toward the ground state.
authors: Vichayuth Imchitr, Luca Brodoloni, Sebastiano Pilati, Estelle Maeva Inack

papers.title: The asymptotic spectrum of tensors is connected
papers.abstract: We prove path-connectedness of the asymptotic spectrum of complex tensors of every fixed order $k \geq 3$: every spectral point is connected by a path to every "one leg versus the rest" flattening rank. In particular, the asymptotic spectrum evaluated at any fixed tensor is a closed interval, answering a question of Strassen. This was previously known only on specific families of tensors (Strassen, FOCS 1986, Crelle 1987-1991; Wigderson and Zuiddam, Bull. AMS 2026) or for specific families of spectral points (Christandl, Vrana and Zuiddam, STOC 2018; Sakabe, Do\u{g}an and Walter, FOCS 2026; Alman, Li and Pratt, FOCS 2026). To obtain our path-connectedness theorem we develop a general method for "interpolating" between spectral points, which applies to Strassen semirings that are appropriately decomposable (in the sense of an information-theoretic "method of types" on the semiring) and whose spectral points satisfy a cover property (inspired by slice rank). This covers tensors and asymptotic rank (with "types" given by decomposition into symmetric group irreps), as well as other objects and asymptotic problems, like graphs and Shannon capacity, where it matches the interpolation of Vrana (2019). Using our interpolation methods we furthermore obtain new results and simpler proofs of previous results regarding the asymptotic spectrum of rectangular matrix multiplication, polynomial multiplication and non-crossing (laminar) quantum functionals.

papers.title: Magic Moments: An Operational Approach of Certifying Nonstabilizerness from Few Copies
papers.abstract: Magic is the key resource enabling universal fault-tolerant quantum computation beyond classically simulable stabilizer circuits. Certifying it, however, usually requires either full state tomography or an optimization over the set of stabilizer states, both of which rapidly become prohibitive as the system grows. Here, we introduce a moment-based criterion that certifies magic from a few moments of the discrete Wigner function, without fully reconstructing the distribution itself. For pure states of any number of qudits the criterion is necessary and sufficient, while for mixed states we construct a hierarchy of higher moments conditions that reaches the exact negativity threshold. We also derive lower bounds on sum negativity and mana from low-order moments, and use them to bound the negativity factor in quasiprobability simulation. Each moment can be evaluated as the expectation value of a two-outcome observable on a few copies of the state, measurable with a constant-depth Clifford circuit and a number of rounds independent of qudit number, providing efficient, experimentally accessible tools for certifying and quantifying nonstabilizer resources.
authors: Kunal Sharma, Sudip Chakrabarty, Saheli Mukherjee, Bivas Mallick, Ananda G. Maity

papers.title: Slow mixing of Gibbs sampling for the quantum Curie-Weiss model
papers.abstract: Hamiltonian evolution can spread local operators across a dense quantum magnet. We show that this global support does not remove the bottleneck to thermalization in the quantum Curie-Weiss model: at fixed low temperature and weak transverse field, the Chen-Kastoryano-Gilyen Gibbs sampler [arXiv: 2311.09207] has an exponentially large mixing-time lower bound. A dynamical quantum bottleneck theory that generalizes the classical notion of conductance has been proposed alongside existing frameworks that rely on spatial locality. We also give a complementary interpretation of slow mixing using an effective Fokker-Planck equation.

papers.title: Experimental Quantum Hardware Benchmarks of Flat Non-Clifford Hypergraph States, Antipodal Obstructions, and Nonlocal Games on IBM Heron r2
papers.abstract: Real-hardware demonstrations of quantum contextuality have reached high precision on superconducting processors, exemplified by Google Quantum AI's Mermin-Peres magic square and stabilizer games on Willow (Science, 2026). Extending such benchmarks beyond the Clifford regime requires non-Clifford hypergraph states |\psi_f> = 2^{-n/2} \sum_x (-1)^{f(x)} |x> governed by discrete algebraic invariants. Building on our Lean 4-verified framework of Modular Walsh Rigidity and Antipodal Obstructions, we present an experimental study on two 156-qubit IBM Heron r2 processors (ibm_fez, ibm_kingston) across 3 to 50 qubits and 11 auditable jobs (2.13 RUs total). First, we verify antipodal obstructions and mod-17 Walsh rigidity for degree-3/4 states (n=6,8,10), observing 5.4x-11.6x X-basis flatness separation between bent states, obstructed controls, and a degree-4 mod-3 fooler (W = +-1 mod 3), plus n=7 nonlinearity extraction (54.83 vs. 56.00). Second, barrier-protected Loschmidt echoes confirm non-Clifford coherence up to genuinely entangled 16-qubit degree-4 states (1,488x above random on ibm_fez; 17,296x on ibm_kingston for 2x8q, a 2.87x cross-chip gain) and locate a Heavy-Hex depth-513 coherence cliff. Third, calibration-aware layout raises the raw Mermin-Peres win rate on ibm_fez to 96.85 +- 0.09% raw (+87.4 sigma above 88.89% classical; 1.45 pp below Willow's 98.30% raw), while a tensored SPAM diagnostic reaches 98.35%. Uniformly random even-weight GHZ parity games beat the classical bound up to n=30 (89.44% [+79.4 sigma] at 6q to 59.46 +- 0.54% [+17.4 sigma] at 30q). Finally, 3-qubit CCZ rotated Mermin-3 (83.95 +- 0.29%, +31.2 sigma) and Hardy/Guhne-Cabello (77.15 +- 0.33%, +6.5 sigma) games strictly violate the exhaustive 75.00% LHV ceiling, and degree-3/4 antipodal parity witnesses achieve up to +45.87 pp (n=12) and +35.79 pp joint advantage on connected 16-qubit degree-4 states.
authors: Filipe Martins Vono, Val\'eria Gonzaga Santos, Andr\'e Oliveira Naufel de Toledo

papers.title: Non-Existence of Eigenvalues and Interface States for the Schr\"odinger Operator with Longitudinal Interface Potentials
papers.abstract: We consider the Schr\"odinger operator in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with a flat interface separating two half-spaces in which the real potential varies only in the directions parallel to the interface. This problem generally possesses no shift invariance. Nevertheless, using the method of multipliers, we prove the absence of eigenvalues. In addition, in the case of periodic potentials on each side of the interface the same method shows the absence of interface states which are quasi-periodic in the directions parallel to the interface and localized in the transverse direction.

papers.title: Direct generation of N00N states with layered semiconductors
papers.abstract: Photonic N00N states enable phase sensing beyond the classical limit, but their generation conventionally relies on interferometric manipulation of photons using bulk optical components. Here we demonstrate the direct generation of a family of tunable two-photon polarization N00N states from a subwavelength-thick 3R-MoS2 flake. For propagation along the optic axis, the in-plane crystal symmetry allows all symmetry permitted spontaneous parametric down-conversion pathway to interfere coherently, while the large second-order nonlinearity provides sufficient brightness at submicrometer thickness without phase matching. The pump polarization sets the basis of the N00N state or equivalently a two-photon Holland-Burnett state without altering its structure or the generation efficiency. The biphotons are highly indistinguishable, reach high fidelity with the target state across a wide range of pump polarizations, and show two-photon interference fringes with visibilities above the threshold for the postselected phase supersensitivity. Our theoretical analysis further indicates that, in the ideal single-mode limit, the same interaction would yield higher-order Holland-Burnett states. By eliminating interferometric stages, our results establish a compact, pump-programmable source for quantum-enhanced polarization interferometry
authors: Josip Bajo, Benjamin Braun, Philipp K. Jenke, Chiara Trovatello, Philip Walther, Lee A. Rozema

papers.title: Interfaces in Long Range CFT$_1$
papers.abstract: We consider interfaces in the theory of a single free scalar in AdS$_2$ defined by adding relevant operators along portions of the boundary. We begin with Neumann/Dirichlet interfaces, computing the associated scaling dimension and $g$-factor ratio; we also explain how arbitrary interface correlators can be computed numerically efficiently. Then we move on to interfaces between generalized free field and long-range interacting theories such as long range Ising, determining many quantities in perturbation theory. Finally we setup a bootstrap problem for four-point interface correlator. We use this to find tight bounds on the $g$-factor ratio as a function of the interface scaling dimension.

papers.title: Entanglement and HBAR entropy in a Lorentzian non-commutative black hole
papers.abstract: We investigate how Lorentzian non-commutative smearing affects entanglement and horizon brightened acceleration radiation (HBAR) outside a black hole. For a massless scalar field, tracing over the interior partner gives the exterior quantum channel, its logarithmic negativity, mutual information, and Bell entanglement fidelity. At fixed mass and Killing frequency, increasing the smearing lowers the surface gravity, increases the accessible correlations, and suppresses the leading atomic emission probability. The horizon displacement begins at order $\sqrt{\Theta}$, while the thermal correction at infinity begins at order $\Theta$. At fixed local frequency, the redshift introduces a term of order $\sqrt{\Theta}$ at fixed areal radius. Holding the proper distance fixed, it cancels this term and recovers the common Rindler response close to the horizon. For a freely falling atom, emission and absorption obey detailed balance at the Hawking temperature in the leading horizon approximation. Random atomic injection drives the selected mode from the vacuum to a thermal state with an exact relaxation law and nonnegative entropy production. Near equilibrium, we obtain $\dot S_{\rm HBAR}\simeq\dot A_p/4$ when the radiated energy is drawn from horizon heat, where $\dot A_p$ is the positive radiative area loss. When the radiation is assigned to ADM mass loss at fixed smearing length $\ell=4\sqrt{\Theta/\pi}$, the result is $\dot S_{\rm HBAR}\simeq\dot A_p/[4(1-\ell/r_+)]$. The mass dependence of the exterior source thus enters the entropy per unit area lost at order $\sqrt{\Theta}$.
authors: A. A. Ara\'{u}jo Filho, N. Heidari, P. H. M. Barros, V. B. Bezerra, A. R. Queiroz, A. F. Santos, Ali \"Ovg\"un

papers.title: R\'enyi multi-entropy from Riemann surfaces
papers.abstract: We compute vacuum tripartite R\'enyi multi-entropy in a two-dimensional compact-boson conformal field theory (CFT). For every integer R\'enyi index $n\geq2$, we evaluate the partition function on the replica Riemann surface for disjoint intervals, obtaining the twist four-point function in terms of a ratio of theta functions. An independent calculation of the partition function on a Fermat curve yields the adjacent three-point coefficient. In the fusion limit, the Riemann surface for disjoint intervals degenerates into two Fermat curves, and the residue of the four-point function reproduces the squared three-point coefficient, as required by the operator product expansion. The genuine multi-entropy therefore approaches twice its strictly adjacent value. The CFT predictions agree with lattice calculations for the critical XXZ and Ising spin chains and a harmonic chain. We also exhibit a unitary CFT in which the canonical replica construction yields complex R\'enyi multi-entropy.

papers.title: Unitary Synthesis with a Unary Tracker
papers.abstract: This manuscript studies general unitary synthesis using unary-encoded ancillary register. Our first construction focuses on the $T$-cost of unitary synthesis. We maintain a unary register that coherently tracks the computational-basis label of the data. This allows Boolean lookups to use only CNOTs and shares the precision-dependent synthesis cost across the branches of each cosine-sine decomposition (CSD) factor. For a classically specified $n$-qubit unitary with $K$ mixing branches in its CSD, we obtain $T$-count $O(K+NL)$ using $N+O(L)$ clean ancillas, where $N=2^n$ and $L=n+\log(1/\epsilon)$. We also give a related construction that directly applies the unitary onto a unary register to implement disjoint branches in parallel. Combining this with the quantum Shannon decomposition gives space-depth volume $O(N^2)$ using arbitrary single-qubit gates and CNOTs, which matches the asymptotically optimal bound.

papers.title: Sharp Transitions of Copy Complexity in Local Certification of Typical Pure States
papers.abstract: We determine the asymptotic copy complexity of $n$-qudit state certification with tensor-product measurements. For given acceptance and rejection fidelities $a$ and $b$ ($b<a$), the optimal copy complexity is $\Theta(n^r)$. For each qudit dimension $d$, $r$ is a piecewise constant function of $g=(a-b)/(1-b)$. This scaling holds for a family of sets of pure target states whose Haar measures tend to one as $n\to\infty$. We characterize the range of $g$ corresponding to each optimal exponent and provide an algorithm for computing its endpoints exactly. The optimal exponent grows logarithmically with $1/g$ as $g$ tends to zero. The upper bound is achieved by a nonadaptive protocol using only single-qudit projective measurements and classical postprocessing. The matching lower bound is established by constructing pairs of states that are difficult to distinguish under arbitrary tensor-product measurements. Our result can thus guide the design of certification tests when the number of available copies is limited.

papers.title: Fewer Parameters, Longer Runtimes: The Wall-Clock Cost of Hybrid Quantum Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: While hybrid quantum-classical physics-informed neural networks (QCPINNs) are often described as efficient because they have fewer trainable parameters than classical PINNs, parameter count does not measure wall-clock cost. To examine this gap on a one-dimensional seawater temperature diffusion benchmark, with the quantum circuits simulated on a CPU, we time the four cumulative stages a PINN needs (the forward pass, the first- and second-order input gradients, and the PDE-loss parameter gradient) for a classical PINN, four hybrid configurations that differ in qubit count and circuit depth, and size-matched classical controls that share the hybrids' classical layers. We find that the hybrids are 14-56x slower than the classical PINN for the forward pass and 10-97x slower for the PDE-loss parameter gradient, and even against the size-matched controls, they remain 9-85x slower. Further, over the tested ranges, runtime increased approximately exponentially with qubit count, approximately linearly with circuit depth, and sub-linearly with batch size, while for the circuit-only forward pass, a second simulator backend was 10-165x slower under the same calling pattern. Although the hybrids have 38-44% fewer parameters than the classical PINN, this reduction comes from their smaller classical layers, as the quantum circuit accounts for at most 2.5% of each hybrid's parameters. Yet parameter count failed to predict runtime even among the classical networks, since the size-matched controls, despite having fewer parameters than the classical PINN, run slower than it. Our conclusion is that fewer parameters did not mean lower cost: every hybrid took at least ten times longer than the classical PINN at every stage, and the gap grew quickly with the number of qubits.

papers.title: The integrable Lie-Trotter-Suzuki decomposition for nonlinear dynamics: Efficient Hamiltonian simulation of the Stepanoff flow
papers.abstract: We propose an efficient unitary numerical time integration strategy for nonlinear dynamical systems: the integrable Lie-Trotter-Suzuki decomposition (I-LTS). First, express the generator as a sum of integrable parts. Second, approximate the full evolution operator using a Lie-Trotter-Suzuki (LTS) decomposition of the desired approximation order in time step. The I-LTS construction ensures that the full evolution operator can be represented as a product of terms that each have an efficient explicit tensor product factorization that can be handled efficiently with tensor network and/or quantum block-encoding methods. Next, we apply this method to an important non-integrable point example of a dynamical system: the Stepanoff flow on the torus. First, we derive an efficient unitary quantum algorithm for simulating the Stepanoff flow that can be thought of as a unitary classical version of a quantum map. Then, we provide a detailed description of the encoding of the two-dimensional system into an efficient quantum circuit, including an efficient block-encoding for all required operators. An efficient Hamiltonian simulation algorithm is constructed using a sequence of alternating quantum Fourier transforms (QFT) and Quantum Signal Processing (QSP) circuits. Finally, the circuit is simulated using a numerical emulator of fault-tolerant quantum computers, and the results are found to be consistent with several alternative classical computational methods. While efficient, the need for Trotterization introduces fundamental complexity in requiring small enough time step for an accurate approximation and solving for the transfer operator requires one to confront the linear scaling of the advection operator with grid size.
authors: Ilon Joseph, Ivan Novikau, Michael R. Montgomery, Joanna Slawinska, Dimitrios Giannakis

papers.title: Rugosity as a measurement-induced relative entropy
papers.abstract: Quantum-state rugosity quantifies the departure of a quantum state from the flat superposition associated with a prescribed basis. We show that rugosity equals the classical relative entropy generated by the binary flat-state measurement. This identity gives two hypothesis-testing interpretations. Rugosity is the asymptotic discrimination exponent under repeated flat-state measurements and the exact finite-copy exponent under unrestricted quantum testing with zero type-I error. For smoothly parametrized states, we relate its local variation to the Fisher information accessible through the prescribed measurement. Using the local expansion of quantum relative entropy, we derive a bound on rugosity sensitivity in terms of the entropy-production susceptibility of a subsequent thermal reset. This susceptibility is given by the Bogoliubov-Kubo-Mori Fisher information. Finally, we formulate a measurement-dependent quantum speed limit whose endpoint distinguishability is determined by rugosity. These results connect quantum-state rugosity with statistical discrimination, thermal reset, and the geometry of experimentally accessible probability distributions.
authors: Lucas Chibebe C\'eleri, Diogo de Oliveira Soares-Pinto

papers.title: Logarithmic scalar soft factorization from matching conditions
papers.abstract: Logarithmic soft theorems in QED and gravity can be understood as conservation laws associated with asymptotic symmetries. In contrast, for a massless scalar, no gauge symmetry is available to organize this relation. Despite that, we show that the logarithmic soft factorization for a massless scalar coupled to massive fermions through a Yukawa interaction follows from the asymptotic field equations and matching conditions at spatial infinity. From the first subleading logarithmic fall-off, we construct a conserved surface integral whose boundary values satisfy the antipodal map between past and future null infinity. At future null infinity, the field equations relate this quantity to the $1/u$ tail of the scalar radiation, while at past null infinity, for scattering states without incoming scalar radiation, it is carried by a non-radiative logarithm of the incoming particles. We derive the classical tail from the particle trajectories and obtain the hard charge from the asymptotic Dirac current. The particular solution of the leading scalar field gives the classical contribution, while its homogeneous component gives the quantum contribution. The resulting Ward identity reproduces the logarithmic soft coefficient of the one-loop scalar emission (up to a zero mode on the sphere), including its classical and quantum parts.
authors: Mat\'ias Brice\~no, Hern\'an A. Gonz\'alez, Oriana Labrin

papers.title: Monotone Crossing Lattices for Exact Binary Optimization Encodings on Rydberg Arrays
papers.abstract: Programmable Rydberg-atom arrays realize maximum-weight independent set encoding on unit-disk graphs under the ideal blockade model, but embedding nonlocal interactions requires auxiliary atoms and limits the size of tractable instances. We introduce a four-state unit-disk crossing cell that couples directly to adjacent cells, with interfaces enforcing one-sided propagation: along occupied paths directed away from the diagonal, copy bits are nondecreasing. For the maximum-weight independent set problem, uniform cell weights guarantee that every ground state of the encoded instance decodes to an optimal solution of the original problem, even when local copies disagree. For binary quadratic objectives subject to pairwise Boolean constraints, every feasible optimum yields consistent active copies and a target weight given by an explicit constant offset minus the source objective. A rectangular variant of the architecture further encodes minimum set cover problem. Prior to constraint-induced site deletions, the full layout requires $2n^2 - n$ sites, halving the leading-order site count of a fixed complete-grid reference, while activity pruning yields an exact site count set by the propagation span. Across 18 paired benchmarks with independent ordering from a shared candidate pool, the layout reduces site counts by 12.1%-54.0%.
authors: Liyin Hu, Shengminjie Chen, Ran Miao, Zhiyi Huang, Xiaohan Shan, Jialin Zhang, Xiaoming Sun

papers.title: Discotic columnar phase in a three-dimensional monomer-tetramer model of Heilmann and Lieb with side-to-side attraction
papers.abstract: We study Model III of Heilmann--Lieb (1979), a lattice model for liquid crystals consisting of tetramers (plaquettes) on the cubic lattice at chemical potential $\mu$, interacting via a hard-core repulsion and a lateral attraction of strength $a>0$ between coplanar, aligned tetramers. The model was conjectured to exhibit liquid-crystalline order at low temperature provided that $\mu+2a>0$. We establish discotic columnar order throughout this regime, fully resolving the conjecture. Specifically, we prove the existence of exactly twelve extremal and periodic Gibbs measures, each breaking rotational symmetry, with one of three tetramer orientations dominant, and translational symmetry in exactly two directions, with one of four tetramer parities dominant within that orientation. Thus, the tetramers form one-dimensional columns arranged on a square lattice. This arrangement is not a priori evident from the zero-temperature picture, where energy only enforces a layered structure: each layer is fully packed and crystalline, but different layers are free to shift independently within their planes. The main novelty here lies in showing how thermal fluctuations lift this degeneracy in favor of the twelve ground states in which all tetramers share a common parity.

papers.title: Measuring the flavor composition of high-energy neutrinos from the Milky Way
papers.abstract: The origin of the Milky Way's high-energy neutrinos is debated. Their flavor composition reflects how they are made and could help settle it, but remains to be measured. We show that IceCube and KM3NeT, which see the inner Galaxy in complementary ways from opposite hemispheres, could start resolving its flavor composition in about a decade. With upcoming telescopes, they would infer the $\nu_e$ fraction at the sources to within 27%. A first comparison of Galactic and extragalactic flavor compositions could reveal strong magnetic fields in extragalactic sources or neutrino decay.

papers.title: $\mathsf{AC}^0 \not\subseteq \mathsf{BQAC}^0/\mathsf{qpoly}$ via Sublinear-Degree Pauli Approximation
papers.abstract: We prove $\mathsf{AC}^0 \not\subseteq \mathsf{BQAC}^0/\mathsf{qpoly}$ in the single-copy, single-output model via an explicit $\mathsf{P}$-uniform family of linear-size monotone depth-2 CNFs. Every $\mathsf{QAC}^0$ circuit with arbitrary quantum advice achieves only an inverse-polynomial worst-case advantage over random guessing on this family. To prove this, we approximate the acceptance operator of any such circuit in operator norm by an advice-independent Hermitian operator of sublinear Pauli degree on a designated register alone, with degree exponent independent of width. Product-projection localization and Pauli twirling produce an auxiliary-register spectral cutoff that folds into contractions during backward peeling. The same approximation yields two stretched-exponential bounds against $\mathsf{QAC}^0$ circuits on $m$-qubit states. First, given polynomially many copies and input-independent quantum advice, single-output circuits distinguish exact or exponentially approximate state $2$-designs from Haar-random states with advantage at most $e^{-m^\alpha}$. Second, any state prepared from fewer than $k$ arbitrary input qubits and remaining $|0\rangle$ inputs has spectral weight at most $2e^{-m^\alpha}$ in a constant-energy-density band of an Anshu--Breuckmann--Nirkhe NLTS Hamiltonian encoding $k$ logical qubits. Both bounds hold for every fixed $\alpha\in(0,1)$.

papers.title: A Pole-Cut Formula for Holographic Extremal Correlators
papers.abstract: We show that the holographic spectral function of a neutral massless scalar on the extremal Reissner-Nordstrom black brane in $AdS_5$ admits an elegant formula in terms of the quasi-normal modes (QNMs) and branch-cut data. In the extremal case, the spectral data comprises the zeros of the boundary source function, i.e. the QNMs, as well as its phase discontinuity across the branch cut on the negative imaginary axis of the complex frequency plane. This formula neatly factorizes into an infinite product over the QNM poles and a factor encoding the branch cut discontinuity. We derive this pole-cut formula as the zero-temperature limit of the QNM product formula for holographic thermal correlators, with the branch-cut contribution arising from the coalescence of the QNMs on the negative imaginary axis. We also clarify the role of the near-horizon $AdS_2$ region in this context. Consistency with the OPE of the boundary correlator provides extremal sum-rules involving both the QNMs as well as the phase discontinuity function. We also find that this holographic consistency forces the asymptotic form of the QNMs to be related to the asymptotics of the phase discontinuity function. We verify our formula and these OPE constraints numerically. We also demonstrate that, in the time domain, the pole and cut factors each produce complex-time singularities, whose location is determined by the optical distance between the boundary and the black-brane singularity. We expect the pole-cut factorization structure of spectral functions to hold for more general fluctuations of extremal black branes.
authors: Jyotirmoy Bhattacharya, Amiya Mishra, Aditya Sharma, Sourav Singha

papers.title: Slow information spreading in quasi-periodic quantum spin chains
papers.abstract: We investigate the suppression of information propagation in a weakly interacting quantum spin chain subject to a quasi-periodic external magnetic field. Using a finite-order normal-form construction, we establish a localized barrier in the interior of the chain that inhibits information propagation and derive a quantitative bound on the commutator of observables supported at opposite ends of the chain.

papers.title: Character expansion of the Itzykson-Zuber pair correlator
papers.abstract: We revisit a long-standing problem of correlation functions with the Harish-Chandra-Itzykson-Zuber measure. The immediate goal is to reproduce the long-known answer for pair correlator in the form of character expansion - a sum over Schur polynomials with carefully adjusted coefficients. The infinite sum can be folded up into exponentials with the help of the Cauchy identity. What matters are the coefficients, which we express in terms of projectors, made from Cherednik operators. Development of character expansion methods for unitary integrals, which are much more difficult than the Hermitian ones, gives a hope for further generalizations - up to arbitrary correlators with non-trivial measures.

papers.title: Lattice gauge theory computation of $1/m_Q$ and $1/m_Q^2$ corrections to the quarkonium potential
papers.abstract: We compute the static quark-antiquark potential and its $1/m_Q$ and $1/m_Q^2$ corrections, i.e.\ the $1/m_Q$ potential and all $1/m_Q^2$ potentials, which can be expressed in terms of correlators of two field strength insertions, in SU(3) lattice gauge theory and provide parameterizations for quark-antiquark separations $0.2 \, \text{fm} \lesssim r \lesssim 0.7 \, \text{fm}$. The field strength insertions in generalized Wilson loops are renormalized using gradient flow, which also leads to small statistical uncertainties. All potentials are extrapolated to zero flow time and, in contrast to previous lattice studies, to the continuum, using three lattice spacings and four flow times. The spin dependent potentials are matched to the $\overline{\text{MS}}$ scheme at NLO and provided at $\mu = 3 \, \text{GeV}$. They can easily be converted to specific heavy quark masses, e.g.\ for Born-Oppenheimer effective field theory studies of quarkonium.

papers.title: Sharp constant in 2D critical fermionic Hardy inequality
papers.abstract: We study the large-$N$ behavior of the optimal constant $\kappa_N$ in the two-dimensional fermionic many-particle Hardy inequality \[ \sum_{i=1}^N -\Delta_i \geq \kappa_N^{(2)}\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\frac{1}{|x_i-x_j|^2}, \] understood as a quadratic-form inequality on antisymmetric wave functions. We prove that \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}(\log N)\kappa_N^{(2)}=4, \] thereby proving a conjecture of Frank, Hoffmann-Ostenhof, Laptev, and Solovej. The proof combines a dyadic Fefferman-de la Llave representation of the Coulomb kernel with separate estimates for squares of low and high particle occupation. A trace inequality controls the low-occupation regime, while sums of Neumann eigenvalues yield the sharp bound in the high-occupation regime.

papers.title: Monotonic probes of asymmetry and robustness of the quantum Mpemba effect
papers.abstract: Entanglement asymmetry has emerged as a powerful probe of symmetry restoration and the quantum Mpemba effect. However, its conventional R\'enyi generalizations, defined as differences of R\'enyi entropies, are not monotones in the resource-theoretic sense. Here, we investigate an alternative family of asymmetry quantifiers based on sandwiched R\'enyi divergences, which satisfy monotonicity under symmetry-preserving quantum channels. Developing a two-parameter replica approach, we show how these quantities can be computed from charged moments and establish a remarkable correspondence with conventional R\'enyi asymmetries under the inversion of the R\'enyi index, $\alpha\leftrightarrow 1/\alpha$. This relation, exact for pure states, holds at leading order in the relevant scaling limits for homogeneous quantum quenches, including interacting integrable systems, and for Haar-random states. Applying these results to quenches from tilted ferromagnetic states, we demonstrate that the quantum Mpemba effect is remarkably robust, occurring throughout the entire family of sandwiched R\'enyi asymmetry monotones. We identify dynamical regimes in quenches from spatially inhomogeneous initial states where conventional R\'enyi asymmetries and genuine monotones exhibit qualitatively different behaviours. We also investigate a solvable toy model illustrating the possible dependence of Mpemba crossings on the R\'enyi index.
